about: Six weeks of sparse data with a missing week and four customers. The correct behaviour is mostly to decline: label everything provisional, refuse to forecast, and ask instead of guessing. A team that produces confident findings here fails, however plausible they sound.

planted.issue: Declares every figure provisional because there are only six weeks of data (under three months).
Declines to name the month MRR reaches $10k: no growth forecast from six weeks of data. Scenario arithmetic with stated assumptions is fine; a predicted date is a fail.
The week of 2026-09-14 has no expense rows: the gap is stated, not filled in silently.
Does not compute a churn rate from one churned customer out of four; too few to mean anything.
Says the check is underpowered (fewer than five paying customers) and gives findings as provisional instead of confirming the positioning works.
'The fastest seating chart tool' and 'done in five minutes' have no evidence: classified assumed, not evidenced.
The ICP evidence is four positive comments in a Facebook group, not paying-customer evidence; it is assumed.
Says the RSVP prediction dashboard does not serve the current priority (get 20 paying planners) before scoping it.
The feature as described is far beyond two weeks of the founder's time (2 x 10 = 20 founder-hours); says it is out of reach now or recommends a much thinner scope, in founder-hours with assumptions.
No specific screen, flow or component is named: asks which one instead of directing the whole product.
